deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This is a metrics-only commit that mirrors the already-landed MRV1 CUDAGraphStat support (vllm-ascend's model_runner_v1.py already has its own cudagraph_stats/CUDAGraphStat handling). (field-name based, safe). Concrete required adaptation: (1) update tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_manager_v2.py (~line 631) to pass cudagraph_stats=None (and, for robustness against the already-added dp_sync field, dp_sync=None) when constructing vllm_model_runner.ExecuteModelState; (2) optionally add a UT asserting cudagraph_stats is None when cudagraph_metrics is disabled on the NPU V2 runner, mirroring the upstream eplb test change; (3) verify the cudagraph_metrics path works end-to-end with ACL graphs (make_cudagraph_stats uses batch_desc.cg_mode and num_tokens, both available on NPU), no functional adaptation needed. Signed-off-by: Ziming Huang <48115868+ZeldaHuang@users.noreply.github.com>

affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py: DyntraLBScheduler.schedule() (also AsyncDyntraLBScheduler via inheritance) — verbatim copy of upstream padding condition at line 857

vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py: RecomputeScheduler.schedule() (also AsyncRecomputeScheduler / DyntraLBRecomputeScheduler / AsyncDyntraLBRecomputeScheduler) — verbatim copy of upstream padding condition at line 725
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The upstream commit relaxes the spec-decode padding gate in Scheduler.schedule() from `(scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)` to `not prefill_scheduled and (scheduled_running_reqs or num_computed_tokens > 0)`, so that synchronously resumed PD requests (num_computed_tokens > 0, no prior running work this step) are padded to 1 + num_spec_tokens for uniform decode/ACL-graph dispatch. vllm-ascend keeps custom schedulers whose schedule() body is a near-verbatim copy of this logic and still carries the OLD buggy gate. Apply the same two-line change in: (1) vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py:857 and (2) vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py:725 — replace `and (scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)` with `and not prefill_scheduled` / `and (scheduled_running_reqs or num_computed_tokens > 0)`. Both methods already have `num_computed_tokens` in scope at that point. Keep the existing inline budget checks (`num_new_tokens > token_budget or num_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens > self.max_model_len`) used by these copies. Optionally add a regression test mirroring upstream test_spec_decode_padding_resumed_request_without_running_requests in tests/ut/. No interface signature changes (SchedulerOutput unchanged); no patch-catalog updates. Schedulers that inherit upstream schedule() (BatchJobAwareScheduler, ShortRequestFirstAsyncScheduler) and the v0.24.0-pinned patch_balance_schedule.py (no padding logic) are unaffected.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. Behavior change is limited to speculative decode + PD/resume scenarios: resumed requests are now padded to a full 1 + num_spec_tokens decode instead of running unpadded, which is what upstream now does. Until applied, DyntraLB and Recompute scheduling paths on Ascend keep the original bug (resumed spec-decode requests unpadded when they are the first/only work in a step), causing uniform-decode/ACL-graph dispatch fallback and throughput loss in PD deployments (Mooncake/Nixl KV loads). The custom schedulers use slightly different budget guards (token_budget vs request_token_budget) than upstream, so when porting the fix verify the cap behavior for the padding path still matches the intended 1 + num_spec_tokens.

Co-authored-by: Tyler Michael Smith <tlrmchlsmth@gmail.com>

affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/native/offloading_connector.py (AscendOffloadingConnector inherits upstream OffloadingConnector, which constructs the modified OffloadingConnectorScheduler)

vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py (SchedulerOffloadConfig/GroupOffloadConfig refactor, inherited by AscendOffloadingConnector; removes is_store_reachable_swa_chunk/alignment_chunk_count, adds manager_cls/kv_cache_spec/retention_interval/dcp_world_size)
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py (SingleTypeKVCacheManager.reachable_block_mask signature + SlidingWindowManager/MambaManager behavior)
vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mamba_manager.py (AscendMambaManager inherits the modified MambaManager.reachable_block_mask)
vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/coordinator.py (_reachable_block_mask/_get_manager_class consumers of the changed interface)
vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py (register_ascend_kv_cache_specs must keep custom specs resolvable by KVCacheSpecRegistry.get_manager_class)
vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py (write-path reachable_block_mask alignment on SlidingWindowManager)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
All API changes are additive (new optional dcp_world_size=1 kwarg) but the OffloadingConnector scheduler refactor and the new retention_interval feature do affect vllm-ascend's AscendOffloadingConnector, which deliberately reuses the upstream scheduler (see vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py). Concretely:

1. ascend_store/coordinator.py: `_reachable_block_mask` wraps `manager_cls.reachable_block_mask` via getattr + try/except fallback, so it survives the new `dcp_world_size` kwarg, but it does NOT pass `dcp_world_size`. The upstream scheduler now calls `manager_cls.reachable_block_mask(..., dcp_world_size=decode_context_parallel_size)` and `SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask` scales `block_size * dcp_world_size` (with a dense fallback when `alignment_tokens % block_size != 0`). Under DCP with hybrid SWA/Mamba offloading, the AscendStore write-path mask can now disagree with the offloading scheduler's store mask. Pass the effective `dcp_world_size` through `_reachable_block_mask` for consistency.

2. SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec now requires `KVCacheSpecRegistry.get_manager_class(kv_spec)` to return non-None for every group (assert). vllm-ascend registers AscendMLAAttentionSpec/AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec -> FullAttentionManager, AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec -> SlidingWindowManager, KpoolTailSpec -> KpoolTailManager in register_ascend_kv_cache_specs (core/kv_cache_interface.py), which satisfies this today; ensure any future custom KVCacheSpec is also registered, otherwise the AscendOffloadingConnector store path will fail the assert.

3. Validate AscendOffloadingConnector SWA store-scheduling with the new reachable_block_mask-based chunk filtering (removes the old alignment_chunk_count/is_store_reachable_swa_chunk logic). For AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec (block_size 128) the new dense fallback (returns None when alignment_tokens isn't a multiple of the DCP-scaled block size) replaces the previous reachability filtering; confirm store/load hit behavior for SWA + DCP on NPU.

4. retention_interval: the scheduler now reads `vllm_config.cache_config.prefix_cache_retention_interval` (same VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL env var vllm-ascend already uses in ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py, pool_worker.py, patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py) and validates it (non-negative; for SWA groups must be a multiple of tokens_per_chunk). Keep vllm-ascend's own retention handling consistent with this new validation when the AscendOffloadingConnector path is used.
deep_analysis.risk: Low to moderate. No breaking signature changes (all additions have defaults) and no compile failure is expected; vllm-ascend does not reference the removed symbols (alignment_chunk_count, is_store_reachable_swa_chunk, SchedulerOffloadConfig/GroupOffloadConfig directly). Main risks: (a) behavioral divergence in SWA/Mamba chunk reachability between the new DCP-scaled scheduler mask and vllm-ascend's non-DCP-scaled AscendStore write-path mask under decode_context_parallel_size > 1, which could cache or drop blocks inconsistently in hybrid offloading; (b) the new `assert manager_cls is not None` in the offloading scheduler fails for any unregistered custom KV cache spec; (c) the new retention_interval validation in SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec may reject previously-accepted configurations. These only manifest in the KV offloading / PD-disaggregation paths, not in normal single-instance inference. The upstream mooncake/store/coordinator.py change (dcp_world_size=1) has no direct impact since vllm-ascend uses its own AscendStore coordinator.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This is a brand-new hybrid model architecture (MLA + sparse kpool indexer + KDA linear attention + MHC + MTP spec decode + multimodal vision). The upstream commit is CUDA/ROCm-centric: the nvidia path depends on DeepGEMM paged-MQA kernels (PAGED_MQA_PAGE_SIZES in vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py), csrc cache kernels, fwht128 fp8 kpool compress, and the new FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90/FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE/FLASHMLA_SPARSE backends; the AMD path reimplements kpool_compress/KDA in Triton under vllm/models/glm5next/amd/. vllm-ascend must do the same on NPU:

1. Model port: implement vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/ (model.py, attention.py, kda.py, mtp.py, multimodal.py, processor.py, sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py, kv_cache.py, config.py) and register the three architectures in vllm_ascend/models/__init__.py so they override the upstream CUDA registry entries.
2. Config patch: add patch_glm5next_config.py (loaded from vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py) to register Glm5NextConfig/Glm5NextTextConfig/Glm5NextVisionConfig in _CONFIG_REGISTRY and to make ModelConfig.is_deepseek_mla return True for model_type glm5_next/glm5_next_text (upstream hardcodes the MLA model_type tuple and cannot know downstream architectures).
3. KV cache: mirror the upstream KpoolTailSpec + KpoolTailManager (1-block circular, no-prune, prefix-cache-exempt scratch for the in-progress kpool) in vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/kv_cache.py and register them from NPUPlatform.register_custom_kv_cache_specs via vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.register_ascend_kv_cache_specs. Propagate the new MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size field through AscendMLAAttentionSpec and keep cache_dtype_str consistent in merge().
4. Block-size alignment: honor the upstream Platform._get_indexer_block_alignment hook (default returns None - the CUDA override returns index_kpool * min(PAGED_MQA_PAGE_SIZES)); Ascend should either implement its own override in NPUPlatform or align cache_config.block_size to index_kpool multiples so chunked-prefill stays pool-aligned and the kpool indexer asserts hold.
5. Attention backend selection: in NPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls, keep the MLA backend for GLM-5.3-Flash (index_kpool) rather than routing to SFA; adapt the indexer metadata builder usage to the new per_req_decode_lens/decode_is_uniform/max_prefill_seq_len fields and the kernel_block_size-based indexer block-table compression added to DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder.
6. Ops: implement Ascend kpool-compress (fp8, Hadamard-128, gate weighting), KDA recurrent ops, MHC pre/post ops, fused_eh_norm, causal_conv1d, and the tail-cache read/write kernels in vllm_ascend/ops/ and vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/ops/.
7. Runner/worker integration: teach model_runner_v1.py and worker/v2/attn_utils.py to recognize Glm5NextIndexerCache/Glm5NextTailCache (is_glm5_next_kpool_cache) so they keep their own KpoolTailSpec instead of being converted to AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec, and handle kpool KV allocation/reshape in initialize_kv_cache.
8. Spec decode: extend vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py for Glm5NextMTP draft heads (n_predict from num_nextn_predict_layers, logit_hidden/recycle_hidden outputs).

Key shared-code contracts to track: MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size (new, must be uniform per KV group), AttentionMetadataBuilder.set_kernel_block_size (new, additive), KpoolTailSpec (new KVCacheSpec subclass), Platform._get_indexer_block_alignment (new classmethod, default None so non-breaking), and the DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder decode/prefill metadata changes in vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py.
deep_analysis.risk: high - the adaptation is a full model port touching every layer of the stack (model definition, KV cache spec/manager, attention backend selection, indexer metadata builder, spec decode, multimodal processing). Risks include: (1) the kpool indexer's block-size multiple requirement (index_kpool*32) interacting with Ascend's fixed 128-token block; (2) keeping the MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size/cache_dtype_str merge invariants consistent across Ascend's converted specs or KVCacheSpec.merge() asserts will fire at startup; (3) the KpoolTailSpec no-prune, prefix-cache-exempt semantics must be preserved or decode/spec-decode/P-D transfer corrupts the in-progress pool; (4) CUDA-graph/ACL-graph capture with the new kernel_block_size path and per-req decode length buffers (dynamic shapes) may need breakable-graph handling; (5) GLM-5.3-Flash is a spec-decode MTP + multimodal model, so correctness of draft/target interaction and vision-tower LoRA/video preprocessing must be validated with model evals on NPU.
